condition: non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction)

key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Acute, over minutes to hours. LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL or left chest. RADIATES to left arm, jaw, neck, back. DURATION: Prolonged >10-20 minutes. CHARACTER: Pressure, squeezing, heaviness. AGGRAVATING: Can occur at rest or with exertion. RELIEVING: Partial relief with nitroglycerin possible. TIMING: Persistent or crescendo pattern. SEVERITY: 6-9/10. KEY POSITIVES: Troponin elevation (positive cardiac enzymes), dyspnea, diaphoresis, nausea, elderly or diabetic patient, cardiac risk factors. KEY NEGATIVES: NO ST elevation on electrocardiogram (ECG) (differentiates from ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) but still myocardial infarction (MI)).
